compile_and_simulation_frontier.reason_tb_watchdog_cannot_help: The #3000000 global watchdog is evaluated only after the Verilog scheduler advances. This attempt is blocked before any observable Verilog time, so the HDL watchdog cannot expire in wall-clock time.
compile_and_simulation_frontier.reason_resource_heartbeat_does_not_prove: The independent bash monitor updates once per second even while simv is blocked; it proves resource-monitor liveness, not Verilog progress.

r17_reference.conclusion: R18 wall time is not credible as workload-dependent RTL simulation time: the smaller R17 TB traversed 1842 reported cover attempts and reached 5,527,500 ps in about 8.7 seconds, whereas R18 has not emitted its first Verilog-time token.

process_and_socket_evidence.interpretation: The main VCS simulation thread is joined on a helper which is polling an established vendor-address HTTP socket with no application response. No CPU or log progress occurs across repeated polls. This is a runtime-library wait, not an RTL combinational loop or a long event queue.

synopsys_path_attribution.reason_not_to_overclaim: The socket belongs to simv and the loaded libraries expose a Synopsys telemetry facility, but a no-attach audit cannot map the helper call stack to one exact proprietary subsystem.

findings.title: R18 is blocked in a Synopsys runtime external-service helper before Verilog execution
findings.evidence: sim.log remains at the 480-byte startup banner; main TID 231606 futex-joins helper TID 231704; helper polls fd10 once per second; fd10 is an ESTABLISHED HTTP connection to 198.182.50.26 with zero application bytes received and no CPU/log progress.
findings.impact: The live attempt cannot produce functional evidence while this state persists. No observed behavior may be attributed to RTL, TB, SVA, coverage, cycles, PPA or energy.

findings.title: The runner has no wall-clock simv watchdog
findings.evidence: The runner invokes ./simv directly and waits for PIPESTATUS. Its one-second resource heartbeat remains healthy independently. The TB has a #3000000 simulation-time watchdog, which cannot fire before Verilog time begins.
findings.impact: An unavailable external runtime service can consume the only attempt indefinitely. The successor must add a wall-clock bound without weakening HDL verification.

fail_closed_action.threshold_definition: 30 wall-clock minutes after simv PID 231606 started
fail_closed_action.threshold_rationale: The gate is about 49x R17 total wall time and over 200x its observed simulation time, while still allowing a conservative WAN-recovery window.
root_may_terminate_at_or_after_threshold: sim.log is still 480 bytes with no Verilog-time, coverage, PASS or failure token
both simv thread CPU counters remain effectively stationary
the external helper still polls without receiving application data
resource heartbeat is live and OOM/fail counters remain zero
fail_closed_action.termination_policy: Use the runner's catchable TERM failure path against the complete R18 process group so simv, tee and monitor cannot be orphaned; do not use SIGKILL first. Then require RUN_FAILED_OR_INCOMPLETE.json, FAILED_DO_NOT_CITE, SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.seal.sha256 to exist and verify. If graceful terminal sealing itself fails, quarantine as an unsealed consumed infrastructure failure and never cite or resume the identity.

successor_runner_minimum_delta.documented_switch_source: The current sim.log states that -no_save avoids the ASLR-triggered simv re-execution; the exact TB/RTL/SVA sources contain no $save/$restart/checkpoint use.
successor_runner_minimum_delta.wallclock_rationale: Five minutes is over 34x the observed R17 simulation time and converts another pre-time runtime wait into a deterministic failure receipt.
runner_requirements: Pin and hash any additive runner/whitelist/test changes through a fresh independent source/release/final-hammer chain.
Capture timeout exit status distinctly as infrastructure_timeout_before_verilog_time when sim.log has no HDL progress token.
Preserve the existing exact functional, coverage, P2, six-attack, resource and double-seal gates unchanged.
Do not introduce or recommend an undocumented telemetry-disable environment variable.
Do not infer that -no_save disables external communication; it only removes the documented ASLR re-exec path and the wall-clock wrapper supplies the actual fail-closed bound.
